scope: Source-only Chromium software-WebGL. Controlled cases use Playwright clock emulation for the real production timer loop, independently schedule display callbacks at declared nominal rates, and retain actual source update/render/clock observations. They do not set actor poses, race phases, timer values or physics outputs. The pause lap-notification is a disclosed controlled ID8 event. A separate unmodified real-time sample records host jitter. No full races, builds, packages, native game or existing user session are involved.

visualReview.note: Original course, WhizzKitty kart, roster/minimap/bonus and advancing original lap-time atlas are visible after the authored green transition. This performance-focused browser setup intentionally uses 640x480 and 50% world render scale; it is not a visual-fidelity comparison with native Windows.

observationNotes.cadence: Display schedules include an initial frame at time zero; 31/60/120/144/240 Hz therefore yield 32/61/121/145/241 frames over the inclusive one-second interval. All have the identical separately scheduled 40-update trace.
observationNotes.integerGate: Native admission compares integer GetTickCount-style floors, while its physics interval is floating-point measured time. Thus a raw real-host interval can be slightly below decimal 25ms; the observed consecutive integer starts remain at least25ms.
observationNotes.failureRetained: first-native-cap-failure.json retains the integration failure where an old input guard rejected native float32 0.1. The final source includes the bounded input/recovery-consumer guard correction and its regression tests.
